subject: Compatibility between EARS' curated XVF3800 interface and reSpeaker Flex.

result.summary: Flex uses the same XVF3800 vendor-control architecture. All commands used by the current EARS read-only module match the official Flex full host table.

usb_discovery.official_flex_behavior: The current Flex scripts default to vendor-only discovery and allow an explicit PID because firmware profiles may expose different PIDs.
usb_discovery.compatibility_risk: A non-0x001A Flex profile would not be discovered by the current EARS open() method.
usb_discovery.recommended_change: Later add enumeration by vendor with an explicit allowlist and product-string verification; never silently bind to the first XMOS device.

upstream_inconsistency.issue: The compact Flex DoA demo declares DOA_VALUE as four uint16 values and manually rebuilds bytes, while the full host controller declares two uint16 values.
upstream_inconsistency.canonical_choice: Use the full xvf_host.py table: two uint16 values, azimuth and speech flag.
upstream_inconsistency.validation_needed: Capture one raw USB response from physical Flex hardware and record payload length and bytes.

compatibility_boundaries: Protocol compatibility does not make firmware images interchangeable.
Circular and linear arrays require geometry-specific firmware.
USB and I2S firmware have different DFU paths and transport behavior.
Do not expose SAVE_CONFIGURATION, CLEAR_CONFIGURATION, REBOOT, or DFU through the passive EARS telemetry class.
Six-channel USB mode changes the audio stream shape but not the selected passive control commands.
